verdict: 1) R1/R2 = 1 kOhm pull-ups give tr = 19.74 ns on the 23.3 pF 46.6 mm I2C bus (well below the 120 ns Fm+ ceiling, whereas 4.7 kOhm would fail at 92.84 ns). 2) Because In2.Cu (CS/SW) sits only 0.21 mm from B.Cu (I2C_SDA) vs 1.29 mm from In1.Cu GND, factory-default AW20198 SRCR=0x02 (1 ns rise) injects 162.9 mV glitches into I2C_SDA; programming SRCR=0x07 (6/10 ns) + PCCR=0x02 (3-Phase) + SSCR=0x15 cuts I2C glitches 3.39x to 48.1 mV and drops 300 MHz radiated EMI by 30.4 dB! 3) DGCR=0x44 clamps off-row Red LED peak forward voltage from 2.196 V (visible ghost flash!) down to 1.935 V (< 1.65 V turn-on).
